title: The wives who left the sacrifice
hook: learned priests ignore Krishna; their wives bring the food
carry: pure bhakti: love with nothing laid on top
tomorrow: a king is offered any boon and asks for ears. why?

segments.voice: Last week ended on the chart of Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu, where every feeling has a place. A new week, and Rupa stops charting and starts defining. First, a story he knew by heart.

A hot afternoon in the Bhagavata Purana. Krishna and the cowherd boys are out with the cows, and the boys are starving. Krishna sends them to some priests nearby, busy with a great fire sacrifice. Go ask for food, he says. Use my name. The priests barely look up. They're learned, the ritual is long, and a few hungry farm boys don't fit in it. So Krishna sends the boys again, this time to the priests' wives. They fill pots with every kind of food they have and walk straight out to the forest to feed him. Later, the husbands are stung. In paraphrase, they say: shame on our learning, shame on our vows. Our wives had what we didn't.
screen: `HUNGRY BOYS ASK THE PRIESTS.` → `THE PRIESTS DON'T LOOK UP.` → `THE WIVES BRING THE FOOD.`

segments.voice: Rupa Goswami, a student of Chaitanya, wrote a whole ocean of a book on devotion, and early on he defines its highest form in one verse. In paraphrase: the highest bhakti is turning toward Krishna, again and again, in a way he would welcome. It's empty of desire for anything else, and it isn't covered over by knowledge, ritual work and the like. Rupa's word for the turning is anushilana, a steady cultivating, the way someone tends a garden every morning. Now look at the priests. Nothing was wrong with their learning or their fire. It just sat on top. Covered is Rupa's key word. Knowledge and duty can be there in a devotee's life; they just can't smother the love. The wives knew less and wanted nothing back. They simply went. Right after, Rupa quotes an older text, the Narada Pancharatra, for a second definition. In paraphrase: bhakti is serving the lord of the senses with the senses. The wives' hands, their cooking, their walking feet weren't in the way. They were the worship. It's one reason so many Hindu homes still offer food to God first, then share it as prasad.
screen: `TURNING TO KRISHNA, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `NO OTHER WANTING, NOTHING ON TOP.` · `THE PRIESTS' LEARNING SAT ON TOP.` · then, large: `THE SENSES SERVE THE LORD OF THE SENSES.`

segments.voice: If there's food or a drink near you, try what many Hindu homes do. Before the first sip, hold it a moment and offer it: to Krishna, if you pray, or simply in thanks, if you don't. Then, if there's a pen, write one thing you do often, a song, a meal you cook, a message to a friend, and under it, honestly, who it's for. Every name on the pile. Let your eyes rest on the last one.
Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu: the ocean of devotion's nectar. It opens by defining the highest bhakti: turning to Krishna gladly, wanting nothing else, nothing laid on top.
screen: `RUPA GOSWAMI'S BHAKTI RASAMRITA SINDHU — today's word`.

segments.voice: Keep this one: pure bhakti is love with nothing laid on top. The priests had the fire; their wives had the love. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1667 COUNTS.` → `RUPA'S OCEAN · 3 OF 7.` → `TOMORROW: WHY ASK FOR EARS?`

howItsDone: In Gaudiya Vaishnava communities, Rupa Goswami's book is studied with a teacher, and its definition of the highest bhakti is used to look honestly at why one serves. In many Hindu homes, food is offered to God before it is eaten, then shared as prasad.

a hymn to the river Sindhu, sung at dawn
a manual of temple rituals for priests

match.prompt: the opening's definition. tap the pairs.
pairs: a steady cultivating, again and again
knowledge and duty don't smother the love
serving the lord of the senses with the senses

myth: pure devotion means giving up study and duty
Rupa says the highest bhakti isn't covered by them. they can be there; they just don't sit on top of the love.
in the definition Rupa quotes, the senses are the instruments of bhakti
serving the lord of the senses with the senses: the eyes, hands and voice aren't in the way.
for Rupa, bhakti is a feeling that visits once and stays
his word is anushilana, a steady cultivating, done again and again.

fork.setup: the priests are learned and in the middle of a sacred ritual. their wives know less. by Rupa's definition, why do the wives come out ahead?
options: their love wasn't covered by anything, and they wanted nothing back.
learning and ritual are bad, so real devotees drop them.
they happened to cook better food than the priests could offer.
fork.reveal: Rupa doesn't throw out knowledge or ritual. The priests' learning just sat on top of the love. The wives' love had nothing on top of it.

original.note: Sanskrit: the ocean (sindhu) of the nectar (amrita) of bhakti's taste (rasa), the name of Rupa Goswami's book.

trapdoor: what you thought: pure devotion means giving up thinking and doing.
what it means: a steady, welcoming turning toward Krishna, with nothing else wanted and nothing laid on top.
what a scholar hears: Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.1.11, with the Narada Pancharatra quoted just after it; the story is Bhagavata Purana 10.23.
recall: action, done without grasping at its fruit

chat.says: nani signed me up to lead a bhajan at the senior send-off. should i learn what every word means first?
options: learn them if you like. just don't let the studying sit on top of the song.
skip it. Rupa says real devotion drops study and thinking altogether.
yes. the bhajan only counts once you understand every single word.
chat.meaning: Rupa's highest bhakti isn't covered by knowledge or ritual. The priests' learning sat on top of the love; the wives' didn't. Priya's study can stay, under the song.

tie.story: The priests' wives carried food out to Krishna, while their learned husbands, busy with the ritual, never looked up.
tie.friend: Priya can learn every word of the bhajan, as long as the studying doesn't sit on top of singing it for Krishna.
tie.you: what sits on top of something you love?

Rupa Goswami.meaning: a follower of Chaitanya who wrote the Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu

anushilana.meaning: steady cultivating, like tending a garden

Narada Pancharatra.meaning: an older devotional text Rupa quotes for a second definition

Chaitanya.meaning: the singer of Krishna's names whom Rupa followed

prasad.meaning: food offered to God, then shared as a blessing

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.23 (Krishna sends the hungry cowherd boys to brahmins performing a sacrifice; they ignore them; the brahmins' wives bring food to Krishna; the brahmins later lament their birth, vows and learning)
Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.1.11 (the highest bhakti: favorable cultivation of Krishna, empty of other desires, not covered by knowledge, ritual work and the like)
Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.1.12, quoting the Narada Pancharatra (serving the lord of the senses with the senses, freed from labels, pure by being for him)
